subject.title: perf: use a focused OpenClaw prepack profile for diagnostics

question: Should Kova diagnostics use a distinct reduced OpenClaw package, and which runtime files, commands, plugins, and generated assets must remain in that package?
rationale: Source inspection cannot determine the intended release-fidelity boundary, acceptable omissions, or whether the profile belongs in OpenClaw packaging or Kova orchestration; those choices affect what diagnostic results mean.

options.title: Specify a focused release profile
options.body: Define the retained surfaces and benchmark gates first, then implement the profile in OpenClaw packaging and consume it from Kova.

options.title: Keep the full release package
options.body: Continue diagnostics against the ordinary release-shaped artifact and pursue performance improvements only in Kova sampling, setup, and reporting.

options.title: Prototype in Kova only
options.body: Add an explicitly experimental Kova preparation path without treating its results as equivalent to full release diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Specify a focused release profile
recommendation.body: Define the retained surfaces and benchmark gates first, then implement the profile in OpenClaw packaging and consume it from Kova.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the issue and recently implemented the closest diagnostic-performance work.
